results.reason: Issue 1 puts the Section 3.2 90-day deadline at about Aug. 16, 2026. It notes that Schedule 3.12 says only that the Company 'intends' to send the notice, so none was delivered. It says the agreement expires Nov. 14, 2026, two weeks before the Nov. 30 Target Closing, and that the MIPA §3.12(c) rep ('through November 2029') is untrue, exposing Sellers to indemnity and termination claims.

Issue 2 identifies the 100% equity sale as a Change of Control requiring Velloran's prior written consent (DA §14.2), with a termination right under §14.3. It notes the consent is omitted from Sched. 3.6 and therefore falls outside §6.4 and §7.1(d). It recommends obtaining the consent before Closing and amending Sched. 3.6.

Issue 5 notes that SL §1.1 adds New York and Virginia and that DA §19.4 ranks the Side Letter above the DA body. It explains that the non-compete covers six states while exclusivity covers four, and recommends conforming the non-compete or extending exclusivity.

Issue 5 contrasts SL §§6.1–6.2 (New York law, New York County courts) with DA §§18.1–18.2 (Delaware law, Wilmington courts). It warns that a single dispute could split between New York and Delaware, and recommends conforming law and forum to Delaware.
The response states that the Initial Term ends November 14, 2026, citing DA §3.1.
The response states that the Target Closing is November 30, the year being 2026 in context (e.g., 'two weeks before Target Closing' of a Nov. 14, 2026 expiry).
The response refers only to a 'four-state Territory' (DA §1.12). It never names the four states (Delaware, Maryland, New Jersey, Pennsylvania).
The response is a memorandum addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each numbered issue has Where (document and section), Why it matters, and Recommendation sections.
The issues are headed 'Most Significant First' and labeled CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM and LOWER. Section 4 lists 'Items to Raise Promptly' with the client and with Quillon's counsel.
The response says the agreement 'does not renew automatically' and that 'a notice sent now would be late'. It recommends seeking a waiver or amendment instead.
The response states that the Velloran consent is not on Sched. 3.6 and is not covered by §6.4 or §7.1(d).
